note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: ˹At least˺ for ˹the favour of˺ making Quraysh habitually secure—
phrases.text: Tabari reads the opening as a word of wonder: marvel at the favour of God to Quraysh, in the winter journey and the summer journey, and their neglect of worshipping the Lord of this House. Other readings are given, and he settles on this one because the verse must be complete on its own.

phrases.translation: secure in their trading caravan ˹to Yemen˺ in the winter and ˹Syria˺ in the summer—
phrases.text: They had two journeys, the one to Syria in the summer and the other to Yemen in the winter, for trade. In winter Syria was too cold for them, so they went to Yemen instead. Some said they spent the winter in Mecca and the summer in al-Ta'if.

phrases.translation: let them worship the Lord of this ˹Sacred˺ House
phrases.text: Let them stay in their home in Mecca and worship the Lord of this House, and the House is the Kaaba. Tabari tells of Umar pointing at the Kaaba as he recited this.

phrases.translation: Who has fed them against hunger
phrases.text: He fed the people of Mecca, through the prayer of Abraham, who asked: provide them with the fruits.

phrases.translation: and made them secure against fear
phrases.text: The commentators differed. Some said He made them safe from the raids and wars the Arabs feared from one another, and the Sacred Precinct gave them that safety. Others said it means safety from leprosy. Tabari keeps it general, for God did not name one enemy and rule out the other.
